It is rejected and recollection requested
questions.explain: Hemolysis releases potassium from red cells, producing falsely high results, so labs typically reject hemolyzed potassium specimens and ask for a new collection. Spinning again cannot reverse hemolysis.

questions.ref: NHA CPT test plan 2025, Processing (rejection criteria)
questions.q: Why is a clotted lavender tube rejected for a CBC?
options: Clotting raises the glucose result
Clotted blood cannot be labeled correctly
Clots trap cells, giving false counts
The tube changes color when clotted
questions.explain: Clots consume platelets and trap cells, so counts are falsely low and can be unreliable. EDTA tubes must stay anticoagulated by immediate mixing. Glucose is not the concern for a CBC.

questions.ref: NHA CPT test plan 2025, Processing (rejection criteria)
questions.q: A light blue tube for a PT/INR is only half full. What is the likely outcome?
options: Rejection due to excess citrate
Acceptance, since a small sample is enough
Acceptance after adding saline
Rejection only if the patient is a child
questions.explain: An underfilled citrate tube has too much anticoagulant for the amount of blood, which falsely prolongs clotting times. Labs reject such specimens, and adding fluid would make things worse.

questions.ref: NHA CPT test plan 2025, Processing (specimen transport)
questions.q: How should specimens be packaged for transport to the laboratory?
options: Loose in a lab coat pocket for speed
In a sealed bag together with the paperwork inside
Lying flat in an open tray
Upright in a sealed biohazard bag
questions.explain: Specimens travel upright in a sealed, leakproof biohazard bag, with the requisition in the separate outer pocket so paperwork stays clean. Upright tubes help clotting and reduce hemolysis and stopper contamination.

questions.ref: NHA CPT test plan 2025, Processing (specimen transport)
questions.q: Why are tubes transported in an upright position?
options: It keeps the printed labels from smudging
It helps clotting and limits stopper contact
It makes the tubes cool down faster in transit
It mixes additives during transport
questions.explain: Keeping tubes upright lets serum tubes clot properly and keeps blood away from the stopper, which reduces contamination and aerosols when opened. Mixing is done at collection, not in transit.

questions.ref: NHA CPT test plan 2025, Processing (serum and plasma)
questions.q: What is the main difference between serum and plasma?
options: Serum contains fibrinogen; plasma does not
Plasma contains fibrinogen; serum does not
Serum comes from anticoagulated tubes
Plasma is collected only in red tubes
questions.explain: Plasma is the liquid part of anticoagulated blood and still contains clotting factors such as fibrinogen. Serum is the liquid left after blood clots, so fibrinogen has been used up. Serum comes from red or gold tubes.

questions.ref: NHA CPT test plan 2025, Processing (specimen appearance)
questions.q: After centrifugation, a serum sample looks milky white. Which condition does this suggest?
options: Hemolysis
Icterus
Normal serum
Lipemia
questions.explain: Milky or turbid serum suggests lipemia, high lipid content often after a recent meal. Hemolysis looks pink to red, and icterus, from high bilirubin, looks dark yellow. Normal serum is clear and pale yellow.

questions.ref: NHA CPT test plan 2025, Processing (specimen appearance)
questions.q: Serum that appears pink to red after centrifugation most likely indicates what?
options: Hemolysis
Lipemia
Icterus
Excess gel
questions.explain: Pink or red serum indicates hemoglobin released from ruptured red cells, called hemolysis. It can affect potassium, LDH and other tests. Lipemia is milky, and icterus is dark yellow.

questions.ref: NHA CPT test plan 2025, Processing (POCT quality control)
questions.q: Under CLIA, what must be followed when performing a waived point of care test?
options: Any method the user prefers
Only the lab director's verbal advice
The manufacturer's instructions
No instructions, since waived tests are simple
questions.explain: CLIA requires sites performing waived tests to follow the manufacturer's instructions exactly, including quality control steps and storage. Changing the procedure can make the test no longer waived.

questions.ref: NHA CPT test plan 2025, Processing (POCT quality control)
questions.q: Why are control solutions run on a glucose meter?
options: To clean the meter's test port
To calibrate the patient's blood type
To warm the meter before use
To check meter and strip accuracy
questions.explain: Running controls with known values checks that the meter and strips work correctly. Results outside the expected range mean patient testing stops until the problem is corrected. Controls are documented with lot numbers and dates.

questions.ref: NHA CPT test plan 2025, Processing (POCT documentation)
questions.q: Which record should be kept for point of care testing?
options: The patient's favorite collection site
Control results and reagent lot numbers
The price paid for each box of test strips
The color of the meter used
questions.explain: POCT documentation includes quality control results, lot numbers and expiration dates of strips and controls, and patient results, allowing problems to be traced. Costs and device colors are not quality records.

questions.ref: NHA CPT test plan 2025, Processing (specimen storage)
questions.q: A serum specimen will not be tested for several hours. What determines how it is stored?
options: Whatever refrigerator space is available
The patient's stated preference
The lab's stability rules for the test
Room temperature in all cases
questions.explain: Each analyte has its own stability: some specimens are refrigerated, some frozen and some kept at room temperature. Storage follows the laboratory's procedure for the test ordered. Using whatever space is available risks invalid results.

questions.ref: NHA CPT test plan 2025, Processing (centrifuge quality control)
questions.q: Why is centrifuge speed checked and recorded on a schedule?
options: Wrong speed can leave poor separation
Speed affects the patient's fasting status
Speed changes the tube color
It is needed only when the lid breaks
questions.explain: Centrifuges are checked for speed and timer accuracy as part of quality control. A machine spinning too slowly leaves cells in the serum or plasma, and one spinning too fast can cause hemolysis.
